title: THE GLORY OF THE YOUTH
mv: The glory of young men is their strength, And the splendour of old men is their gray head.
mvp: “The glory of young men is their strength, And the splendour of old men is their gray head.” Proverbs 20:29 (NKJV)
assignment: Mention five (5) characteristics of glorious youths (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Being a youth is a season of life marked by strength, vision, passion, and potential. It is a divine gift from God, designed not only for personal growth but for Kingdom advancement. While the world often misinterprets youthfulness as a time for reckless living, Scripture describes it as a season of accountability, consecration, and purposeful impact (Lamentations 3:27; Proverbs 20:29). God has deposited something unique in every young person to manifest His glory on earth. This lesson examines what the glory of the youth is and how it can be used meaningfully for God’s purpose.

Youth is a season of vibrancy, potential, and divine purpose. It is marked not only by physical energy but also by mental acuity, creativity, and flexibility. This strength goes beyond muscles-it encompasses intellectual ability, emotional resilience, and spiritual capacity, which are all gifts from God for fulfilling His purposes and assignments on earth (Jeremiah 1:5).

Young people have a natural ability to see the future with fresh eyes (Joel 2:28). Their hearts are not yet weighed down by the compromises and limitations that sometimes come with age, allowing them to think innovatively, challenge old patterns, and introduce fresh ideas into the church, society, and the Kingdom of God.

Another dimension of youth’s glory is purity: purity of heart, purpose, and conduct (Psalm 119:9). God’s glory is revealed when young people resist sin and choose holiness over compromise, being righteous amid temptation (Genesis 39:7-9; Genesis 41:38-44).

Youth is also a season of zeal-energy and enthusiasm that, when directed toward God’s work, produces great impact (Psalm 69:9; 2 Timothy 2:10). This zeal expresses itself through passion for prayer (Daniel 6:5-11), worship, evangelism (1 Corinthians 9:22; 2 Corinthians 12:15), and service, fuelling revival in homes, churches, campuses, and communities.
In essence, the glory of the youth lies in their God-given strength, purity, vision, and zeal, all of which can be harnessed to advance God’s Kingdom and bring honour to His name.

i: Consecration and Commitment: To preserve the God-given glory, young people must prioritise their relationship with God. Consecration protects from the moral decay, distractions and misuse of glory common in today’s world (Romans 12:1-2).

Avoid Temptations and Distractions: The devil specifically targets young people because of their potential. Many youths today lose their spiritual strength to addictions, immoral friendships, social media distractions, materialism, and peer pressure (Judges 16:1-4, 20-21; Proverbs 4:23). Youths must protect their glory by avoiding environments, habits, and influences that weaken their spiritual life (2 Timothy 2:22).

Productive Use of Talents, Skills, and Energy: Youthful glory must not remain idle. God expects young people to invest their abilities in profitable ventures such as academics, ministry, career development, leadership, creativity, business, and community service (Ecclesiastes 9:10). Youths who use their talents constructively become vessels of influence and excellence.

Submission to Mentorship and Godly Guidance: As youthfulness comes with strength, so does wisdom with counsel (Proverbs 11:14). Young people maximise their glory when they are teachable and humble, learning from pastors, parents, spiritual leaders, and experienced believers. Mentorship helps youths avoid mistakes and accelerate their destiny (Proverbs 15:22).

Living with Purpose and Eternal Focus: Youthful glory shines brightest when aligned with purpose. A sense of purpose prevents wastefulness and brings clarity in decisions (Acts 9:6). Being conscious of eternity promotes choices that honour God and leave a lasting impact on generations.

b.x: The youthful age is a time to shine and manifest God’s glory.

i: Mention four ways to preserve and maximise glory.
